items.title: Why the location of a protest matters | LME 173 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: For more than three decades, Jantar Mantar in New Delhi was where people came to make themselves heard by the political establishment. It is barely two kilometres from the Parliament and the Union government’s offices. Tamil Nadu farmers came here holding skulls. Wrestlers came here demanding accountability. And even the India Against Corruption protest was held at Jantar Mantar. The location mattered. Politicians and bureaucrats could not pretend these people did not exist. Journalists did not have to travel to the outskirts of the city to find them. Ordinary commuters could see them, ask questions and understand what they were protesting about. Now, consider what happens when you move that protest away- somewhere out of sight Now, some people may ask- does the location of a protest matter? Yes, it does And that conversation goes beyond Jantar Mantar and Delhi and even the current protests against Gyanesh Kumar Across Indian cities, governments are deciding where dissent can take place, often in the name of traffic, security and public order. items.title: Nearly one crore less: Karnataka final voter roll lists 4.55 crore electors after SIR
items.summary: Karnataka's final electoral roll was published on Tuesday, October 27, with 99.32 lakh fewer names than the electoral roll as of June 16, 2026. The list released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer has 4,55,00,011 names against 5,54,32,314 names in the earlier roll, showing a decrease of 99,32,303 voters. Speaking at a press conference, Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukumar said those not included in the list could continue to apply. “The electoral roll is on continuous updation; any eligible person can continue to apply using Form 6, 7, and 8. If you have been left out of the final roll, apply using Form 6,” he said. Anbu Kumar also thanked the civic society for their help. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was carried out across all 224 Assembly constituencies in Karnataka. Enumeration forms were generated for the 5.54 crore electors whose names were on the rolls as of June 16, 2026. Of these, 4,46,35,975 electors, or 80.52%, submitted their forms to Booth Level Officers (BLOs). One strand concerned women journalists who say male police personnel sexually harassed and manhandled them at protest sites. For the Centre, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said that the government cannot tell "who is a reel maker, and who is an independent journalist" . He also said no woman should be inappropriately dealt with by the police and objected to a blanket direction. Read charitably, this is an administrative complaint: police at a crowded protest cannot verify everyone holding a microphone. That may be true. The question is what follows from it. Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that the Court will examine the varying levels of protection available to accredited journalists, freelancers, independent journalists and influencers. items.title: Madras High Court dismisses KN Nehru's review plea against order for FIR in cash-for-jobs case
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Monday dismissed a review petition filed by former Tamil Nadu Minister and DMK leader KN Nehru challenging its earlier order directing registration of a First Information Report (FIR) in connection with an alleged cash-for-jobs scam in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department [KN Nehru Vs Inbadurai]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan dismissed the plea seeking reconsideration of the Court's February 20 order directing the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register a case based on material shared by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). CJ SA Dharmadhikari and Justice Arul Murugan The proceedings arose from review petitions filed by Nehru and the State government against the Madras High Court's February 20, 2026 order . The order directed the DVAC to register an FIR over alleged irregularities in recruitment to the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department. items.title: Top 5 Business Analyst Courses to Future-Proof Your Career in 2027
items.summary: Business analysts solve problems, work with data, and use AI to support decisions. But which skills can help you stand out and increase your earning potential? The opportunities are encouraging. IIBA’s 2026 Global State of Business Analysis Report found that certified professionals earn 12% more on average than those without certification, and 69% of the surveyed professionals said AI is positively impacting their careers. The pay potential is strong too: in India, business analysts earn an average of ₹17 lakh a year, with top earners making over ₹50 lakh, according to 6figr.
